D. Significant Noise Impacts
A total of two hundred and seventy-one (271) sites were identified as potentially having the highest probability of noise susceptibility in relation to the proposed improvement. The locations of the suspect noise susceptible buildings and land uses are depicted on Exhibit"12". This exhibit is for graphical representation of the noise study sites in relation to the existing roadway and proposed right-of-way.
There are five (5) zoning jurisdictions involved with the lands adjacent to the proposed Lincoln Highway Improvement. These jurisdictions are:
1. City of Chicago Heights (1055)
2. Village of Matteson (3620)
3. Village of Olympia Fields (4390)
4. Village of Park Forest (4535)
5. Cook County, Bloom and Rich Townships (031) Note: The numbers in () are U.S. Bureau of Census code designations.
Present urban development along Lincoln Highway includes residential areas, retail stores, service industries, highway-oriented businesses and some vacant land. The four (4) communities served by this section of Lincoln Highway each have land use maps prepared by planning consultants, although the plans have not been officially accepted by the communities. A composite land use plan is shown in Exhibit "7" on page I-15. There are no significant amounts of undeveloped land tracks adjacent to Lincoln Highway within the limits of this proposed improvement.
The proposed land use for the area along the improvement is expected to remain basically the same as presently zoned due to the high degree of development in the area. Much of the property along Lincoln Highway is or will be part of a strip development, at least one block deep, primarily involved in automobile-oriented or other highway businesses, interlaced with retail stores. Those residential areas that front on Lincoln Highway presently are developing or can be expected to become business properties within the lifetime of this improvement. Any future land use change is expected to be in conformance with the local plans, goals and objectives.
